workedExamples.title: Example 16.1 — tensile stress in a steel rod
workedExamples.question: EXAMPLE 16.1 — A 500 N force is applied to one end of a cylindrical steel rod of diameter 50 cm. Find tensile stress. GIVEN: F=500 N; r=D/2=25 cm. SOLUTION: stress=force/area=F/(πr²)=500/[π(25×10⁻²)²]=2.5×10⁵ N m⁻².
workedExamples.given: F=500 N; diameter=50 cm; r=25 cm

workedExamples.title: Example 16.2 — Young’s modulus of steel wire
workedExamples.question: EXAMPLE 16.2 — To measure Young’s modulus, a 500 kg load hanging from a 2.4 m steel wire of cross-section 16 cm² stretches it by 0.30 cm. Find (a) stress, (b) strain and (c) Young’s modulus. GIVEN: extension x=0.30 cm=3×10⁻³ m; A=0.16 cm²=1.6×10⁻⁵ m² (as printed); load=500 kg; L=2.4 m. SOLUTION (printed): stress=F/A=5000/(1.6×10⁻⁵)=3.1×10⁸ N m⁻²; strain=x/L=3.0×10⁻³/2.4=1.25×10⁻³; Y=stress/strain=2.48×10¹¹ N m⁻².
workedExamples.given: x=0.30 cm; A=0.16 cm² as printed; load=500 kg; L=2.4 m
